Dodge Challenger Hellcat Redeye Drags Ford F-150 Lightning, It's Close Until It Isn't, Of Course
15 photos
Photo: Wheels / YouTube
The videographer behind the ' Wheels ' channel on YouTube recently took a detour around BMP – aka Bradenton Motorsports Park in Florida for some cool action from the FL2K competition, then got back to The Strip, then switched again to BMP, but now they’re hopefully back for good at Las Vegas Motor Speedway.
So, after the switcheroo back and forth from BMP to The Strip and back again, now it’s time to head back to the Las Vegas Motor Speedway as the videographer caught a couple of unlikely foes trying to bring honor to their respective brands – the Mopar side and the Blue Oval fam.
First, let’s meet the protagonists. In the left lane resides a defunct Ford F-150 Lightning, the battery-electric light-duty full-size pickup truck introduced by the Ford Motor Company in May 2021 as part of the fourteenth-generation Ford F-Series, not any of the SVT versions presented for the ninth and tenth iterations.
Both the commercial-grade and the retail versions of the Ford F-Series with electric power have quickly become resounding failures because of the spectacular failure to achieve the previewed sales levels – Ford was already lowering production in 2024 after abysmal 2022 and 2023 deliveries and then stopped production completely in 2025, writing it off as a bad omen and announcing a next-gen Lightning with an EREV (extended range EV) powertrain.
Meanwhile, in the right lane sits a blue Dodge Challenger identified in the video’s description as an SRT Hellcat Redeye, and the widebody muscle coupe is the impersonation of a very successful third generation for the Mopar vehicle. Sadly, Dodge stopped production in 2023 and focused solely on the new Charger with STLA Large underpinnings and Daytona EV or Sixpack inline-six Hurricane powertrains.
Anyway, it’s a nice contrast at The Strip between the silver EV truck and the dark blue muscle car with a widebody attitude. We all know that EVs can put up a great fight due to their AWD and instant torque, but the Mopar is no slouch, either, so it’s an interesting pairing.
Well, the drivers kept it interesting on the tarmac, too, at least for a while: the humongous pickup truck took off nice and fast at the green light, but the notoriously finicky Mopar didn’t hesitate and darted like an arrow in its lane, so the two of them were tied, neck and neck, as they raced past the Christmas tree.
Alas, it was close until it wasn’t, with the Dodge putting to great use that roaring 6.2-liter supercharged V8 engine and the massive Lightning unable to keep up the pace around halfway, so the Challenger slowly and steadily and inexorably drifted in front of the Ford for an ultimately comfortable win: 10.75s at 126 mph versus 12.67s at 105 mph!
